title: Wall Street Near Record Highs as Fed Hike Bets Fade
summary: Gotrade News - The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,477.31 on Monday, up 1.1%, as traders cut bets on an October Federal Reserve rate hike to about
body_markdown:
As reported by[The Edge Malaysia](https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/820402) , economists polled by Reuters had expected a gain of 90,000.


The table below sets out the last three monthly payroll prints from the BLS release, with the September consensus from The Edge Malaysia's report.

Consensus: +90,000


Stocks first reacted on Friday, when the Nasdaq rose 1.19% to 27,190.86 and the S&P 500 gained 0.73%, per The Edge Malaysia. That report cited CME FedWatch odds of an end-of-October hike at 22.7%, down from 64.2% a week earlier.


"Today's news was OK insofar as it means the economy isn't roaring... cautious optimism is kind of where people are," said Robert Bernstone, head of trading at SummitTX Capital, as quoted by The Edge Malaysia.


A December increase remains largely priced in, according to Investing.com, so the repricing so far applies mainly to the October meeting. The 10-year Treasury yield stood at 5.31%, near its highest level since 2002, the same report said.


That backdrop follows the move covered in our earlier piece on how the[jobs report tested stocks after a yield spike](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/jobs-report-tests-stocks-after-yield-spike/) .


## What Comes Next for Stocks After the Nasdaq Record?


The next test arrives Wednesday, when the Federal Reserve publishes the minutes of its September meeting, per Investing.com. PepsiCo and Delta Air Lines also report this week, events laid out in our[US market outlook on Fed minutes, PepsiCo and Delta earnings](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/weekly-economic-outlook-2026-10-05/) .


Third-quarter results from the major US banks begin next week, according to Investing.com, giving investors fresh data to weigh alongside rate expectations; a primer on[how to read an earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) covers the figures to watch.


Oil also eased, with Brent crude down 2% on Monday after Middle East exports increased and G7 nations pledged to boost supply, the same report said.
